title: Rewind to the budget origin
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a finite schedule-alphabet word. For any base configuration on $x$, input-head position, integers $u,g$, Boolean word $w$, and unary-counter and guide tapes, starting in budget-start phase with the budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape for $w$, after exactly $|w|+2$ steps the machine is in append phase with counter $0$ and budget head at cell $1$; the base data, input-head position, unary tape and head, guide tape and head, and captured clock tape are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: schedule input x and base configuration
replaced:
From a setup configuration in the budget-start phase with budget head at cell $|w|+1$
(one cell beyond the captured clock tape of the bit word $w$), exactly $|w|+2$ steps
reach the first append phase with budget head at cell $1$; the cost depends only on the
width of $w$, not on its bits, and all tapes and all other heads are unchanged.
